notes: This local reference is treated as the strongest currently recovered author-adjacent implementation source.
Only definitions directly present in this reference can currently be classified as exact-to-reference.

definitions.name: info_spectra
definitions.paper_role: Sequential perturbation contribution table for graph edges or vertices.
evidence: Uses C(G) - C(G-e) or C(G) - C(G-v) sequential deletions.
Returns one row per perturbed element.

definitions.name: info_signature
definitions.paper_role: Information spectra sorted decreasingly by information contribution.
evidence: Implements descending sort on contribution values.
Tie-breaking is deterministic but not semantically material to the descending-rank definition.

definitions.name: inforank
definitions.paper_role: Rank of perturbed elements by descending information contribution with min-tie handling.
evidence: Uses min-tie ranking to mirror algodyn ties.method = min.

definitions.name: relative_reprogrammability
definitions.paper_role: Median absolute deviation of the information signature divided by its maximum value.
evidence: The recovered local algodyn reference implements MAD(signature) / max(signature).
The main paper text states Pr(G) := MAD(sigma) / max(|sigma|).
The project now exposes both variants explicitly.
open_questions: Without the missing supplement-level operational definition, it is unresolved whether the paper text or the recovered local reference is the authoritative implementation target.

definitions.name: absolute_reprogrammability
definitions.paper_role: Balance between positive and negative contribution regimes in the information signature.
evidence: Current implementation uses trapezoidal areas over sorted positive and negative magnitudes.
open_questions: No direct author-adjacent implementation is currently present in reference/algodyn/R.
Supplement-level formula and normalization must still be matched before exact biological reprogrammability claims are made.

definitions.name: combined_reprogrammability
definitions.paper_role: Joint reprogrammability magnitude combining relative and absolute components.
evidence: Current implementation uses Euclidean norm sqrt(rel^2 + abs^2).
open_questions: No direct author-adjacent implementation is currently present in reference/algodyn/R.
Supplement-level definition still needs exact corroboration.
